description:
A package manifest states the packages it depends on, so a package can carry a delta over another rather than a copy of it.

## Background

The manifest rejects unknown keys, with the explicit comment that future composition syntax cannot silently enter the v1 contract. A dependency declaration is therefore a deliberate change to that contract rather than an additive field that slips in, and it carries a schema regeneration: the manifest schema is public through the package's machine-readable inspection output and through the agent-facing bridge over it.

The declaration is what makes two packages legitimate. Without it, a package needing another's vocabulary has to restate it, and the two copies are held equal by an assertion — the shape this container exists to remove.

This states the dependency. Resolving and applying one is separate work, so a manifest declaring a dependency parses and reports it here, and acquires its meaning when the resolution that reads it lands.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A package manifest declares the package ids it depends on, and a manifest declaring none parses exactly as it does today.
- [hard] REQ-02: A malformed or self-referential dependency declaration is rejected where the manifest is parsed, naming the offending entry.
- [hard] REQ-03: The declaration is carried in the value the package's machine-readable inspection output reports, and the published manifest schema is regenerated from the changed type.
- [hard] REQ-04: A dependency id is a constrained identifier of the same shape as a package id, rejected at parse time when malformed.

## Notes

Nothing here resolves a dependency or changes what application does; a package that declares one behaves exactly as it does today until the resolution work lands.
title: Declare one package's dependency on another
